items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: His name is Leo. He's the last one.

ctx.x: Okay, let's see. Okay, let's see. Okay, and we're at 910 Royal. We're at my apartment where we're sitting and relaxing, and we're just going to chat about jazz. The first thing I wanted to talk about was when you were coming up, what were some of the centers of jazz? What did you think of as being places where there was a lot of jazz?

Well, there was a lot of it. Well, not too many places when I first started in my music career, even when I started learning. But I thought maybe possibly you would want to know the time of my birth, and we'd bring it up to that, and we'd get those questions. Oh, I thought we got on your birth before. I don't know if we did that, Dick. Yeah, okay. I know I was born at 1719 North Robeson here in the old French quarters, and the house still remains there. My daddy lived in there, and I was born in there, and my…

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: and my brother Maurice, then Dutch, then Leo

ctx.x: Imagine. There's a good deal of difference in the ages of the children, because Dutch is much younger than you.

Well, you see, you're counting Dutch, but what about the ones before Dutch? You had my sister, then a brother Stanley, then me, and my brother Maurice, then Dutch, then Leo. I mean, she's the youngest, Dutch?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: Now, Leo is the brother that's living here.

ctx.x: Well, that was a sort of a shock. Because I didn't, I don't think Richard was sick. He just sat apart from me. That's nice that I'm so excited. You never know. Now, the house where I was born in New Orleans is still there. My brother is still living here. I was born in it. My sister was born in it. My sister was dead.
Now, that's Leo. Now, Leo is the brother that's living here.

Now, that's where the 75-year house was. But the family is still there. How many brothers did you have? You see, I have one, two, three brothers. And that name? Leo. Leo, Stan was born next to me. He died here. And there's one billion of these. And that's Leo. My first daughter. And my older sister was named. And named Leo Rita. And it was all three. So, yeah. What? Well, she died here. Yeah.
